summary: This golden set scores 1/25 against the live corpus and the single hit is a negative query passing by returning nothing. It measures nothing. benchmark_rag.py refuses to score against it until it is rebuilt.
defects: MATCHER IS BLIND TO MOST OF THE CORPUS. check_source_match() compares os.path.basename(source). A context entry's source is 'sqlite::context_entry::5830', which basename returns unchanged and which carries no category, title or tag. Context entries are ~73% of the collection, so an expectation like 'Cat05-U' can only match the summary NOTE, never the 10,182 raw entries that dominate retrieval.

QUERIES NAME PEOPLE WHO DO NOT EXIST. 'Alex' is EXAMPLE_THIRD_PARTY_NAME from evelyn_config; 'Jordan' matches nothing in the vault. The queries were genericised for the public repo and the corpus was not, so semantic search has nothing to match on.
EXPECTATIONS THAT CANNOT BE SATISFIED. 'Cat10-U' was never created as a note. 'Local AI' was deleted from the vault on 2026-09-26.

ONE EXPECTATION THE ENGINE IS CORRECT TO REFUSE. 'Psychological Blueprint' is sensitivity: private, and policy is that private notes never reach RAG. The benchmark penalises the engine for obeying its own privacy rule.

THE GROUND-TRUTH MODEL DOES NOT MATCH THE DATA. Fixing the matcher does not rescue it: 'What medications am I on?' expects Cat08-U, but medication facts are spread across nine categories (Cat01-U has 20, Cat05-U has 18, Cat08-U has 9), and retrieval returned Cat01-U among others. 'Expect category N' assumes facts are filed by topic into one category. They are not. This is why the set needs rebuilding rather than repairing.
rebuild_guidance: Scoring belongs with the model-alignment benchmark work, not with retrieval patches. When it is built: score vault-note queries by source (they have real filenames) and fact queries by whether the retrieved TEXT contains the answer; template person names as {USER_NAME}/{ASSISTANT_NAME} so this tracked file carries no real identities and works on any deployment, with a gitignored local overlay for vault-specific queries.

Casual question about a household member — should surface their entries.

queries.notes: Greeting with no information need — should retrieve few/no relevant chunks. This tests noise resistance.
